title: Taiwan Detects 10 PLA Aircraft Sorties, 9 Crossing — Highest Since Sept 18 Drill Window, as Xi Arrives in Washington
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 10 PLA aircraft sorties, 6 PLAN vessels and 6 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24 hours to 6 a.m. (UTC+8) September 23, 2026; 9 of the 10 sorties crossed the Taiwan Strait median line, entering the southwestern and eastern ADIZ sectors. Taiwan's armed forces responded with CAP aircraft, navy ships and coastal missile systems. The tally is the highest sortie count since the Sept 18 Jioupeng-drill window high (28 sorties, 24 crossing) and roughly doubles the prior two days' totals (4 sorties each on Sept 21 and Sept 22), coinciding with Chinese President Xi Jinping's arrival in Washington for a three-day state visit.

title: Taiwan's Domestically Built 'Cheetah' 105mm Armored Vehicle Makes Live-Fire Media Debut in Tainan Hours Before Xi's Washington Arrival
detail: Taiwan's Army held a live-fire media demonstration of its domestically developed 'Cheetah' 8-wheeled 105mm mobile gun system at a training area in Tainan on September 23, 2026, hours before Xi Jinping landed in Washington for his state visit. Maj. Gen. Chen Chien-chung said the production vehicle's height has been reduced roughly 30cm from the prototype shown at the 2023 Taipei Aerospace & Defense Technology Exhibition, with a tighter 9-meter turning radius via three-wheel steering; it engaged moving and stationary targets at ranges up to 1.2km and fired on 90-degree angled targets on slopes. The Cheetah, which reaches 100kph with a 500km range and carries anti-drone countermeasures against quadcopters as a stated priority, is slated for mass production of 178 units beginning 2027 under a roughly $1.7B program. AP's wire coverage framed the demonstration's timing as a display of self-reliant defense capability as Taipei watched the Trump-Xi summit for any sign of change to the paused $14 billion US arms package.

title: Xi Jinping Arrives in Washington for 3-Day State Visit as Taiwan Watches Fate of Paused $14B Arms Package
detail: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington September 23, 2026 for a three-day state visit — his first to the White House in more than a decade — with formal talks and a state dinner set for September 24. Taiwan's government said it would 'continue to maintain close contact with the U.S. Department of War and continue to push forward the arms procurement deal between Taiwan and the U.S., ensuring it proceeds as planned,' according to Defense Ministry spokesperson Maj. Gen. Chiao Fu-chun, even as the $14 billion package remained paused since Trump and Xi's May Beijing meeting. US Sen. Pete Ricketts said Washington needed 'to continue just to again let them know that they're not going to be allowed to take Taiwan by force,' while former Trump deputy national security adviser Matt Pottinger predicted Xi would 'lecture at length' on Taiwan without any substantive outcome. A protester was photographed scaling a light pole near the White House to unfurl a banner opposing Xi's visit.
